items.title: AI Architectures as Variable Epistemic Conditions: Generating Descriptive Spaces in Which New Scientific Questions Become Formulable
items.abstract: Abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used in computational neuroscience for prediction, classification, representation learning, parameter estimation, and related analytical tasks. In most applications, however, the scientific question and the target quantities are specified in advance. Different model architectures may be optimized or compared, but they are primarily evaluated by how well they answer the same predefined question rather than by what different scientific descriptions and questions their architectural differences might make possible. We propose a different use of AI: to treat architectural variation itself as an experimental epistemic variable. Different AI architectures embody different inductive biases and therefore make different temporal, relational, topological, geometrical, symbolic, or dynamical structures accessible in the same empirical data. Rather than asking primarily which architecture performs best on a predefined task, we propose deliberately applying structurally different model families to the same data while minimizing prior commitments about which explanatory quantities should matter — for example entropy, dwell time, recovery time, intrinsic neural timescales, or network connectivity. Each architecture can thereby generate a distinct descriptive space . The primary scientific opportunity lies in architecture-specific discovery. items.title: Ayala Ω Framework H6-D: Preregistered Angular-Acceptance × Initial-Final Interference Stress Test of the Frozen 756–781 MeV Region
items.abstract: The protocol prespecifies a 25 MeV target window (0.756–0.781 GeV) and equal-width adjacent lower and upper control windows, together with the primary acceptance-weighted Ω-window contrast and angular/IFI diagnostic. It also freezes the primary KLOE-II-like small-angle radiative-return configuration, statistical and uncertainty reporting plan, benchmark requirement, anti-tuning rules, reproducibility requirements, and outcome-classification framework. H6-A remains frozen and is not redefined by this analysis. Alternative windows, cuts, observables, generator settings, or other modifications introduced after inspection of the H6-D results will be treated as exploratory. This protocol was frozen on September 2, 2026, before evaluation of the exact H6-D target-window statistics. It does not claim resolution of the muon g−2/HVP discrepancy, discovery of new physics, or proof of a causal mechanism.

items.title: Code and aggregate results for: Impact of induced error on cross-sectional analyses of weight and linear growth in children (Qual-AD 1A)
items.abstract: This archive contains the aggregate results and analysis code for the manuscript "Impact of induced error on cross-sectional analyses of weight and linear growth in children" by Daymont et al. The work is part of a larger study, Qual-AD (Quality of Anthropometric Data), and this analysis is referred to by our team as Qual-AD Study 1A. The study uses artificially induced errors to characterize how measurement error affects cross-sectional analyses of weight and linear growth across 113 error scenarios and 10 age cohorts in two networks, the PaTH PCORnet network and the American Academy of Pediatrics' CER2 network. Contents: Aggregate results at the network level (PaTH and CER2) and for demographic and clinical subgroups, as CSV files. A codebook defining the output columns and a catalog of the simulated error scenarios. The analysis code used for the PaTH network, together with notes describing how the published results relate to the code. The version of the growthcleanr data-cleaning package used for the study, with reference materials.  Individual- and organization-level data are not included because of data use agreements; results are provided by network and by subgroup only, and organization identifiers are removed from the data and redacted in the code to prevent identification of participating organization. An interactive viewer for these results is available at https://carriedaymont.shinyapps.io/qual-ad-cross-sectional-results . Code is released under the MIT License and results under CC-BY-4.0. items.title: Feedforward Closedloop Learning (Error forward propagation)
items.abstract: This release solves the long term stability issues with FCL by applying Oja's rule at neuron level. Thanks to Suraj Prasanth Naranatt who found the solution to this problem. For an autonomous agent, the inputs are the sensory data that inform the agent of the state of the world, and the outputs are their actions, which act on the world and consequently produce new sensory inputs. The agent only knows of its own actions via their effect on future inputs; therefore desired states, and error signals, are most naturally defined in terms of the inputs. Most machine learning algorithms, however, operate in terms of desired outputs. For example, backpropagation takes target output values and propagates the corresponding error backwards through the network in order to change the weights. In closed loop settings, it is far more obvious how to define desired sensory inputs than desired actions, however. To train a deep network using errors defined in the input space would call for an algorithm that can propagate those errors forwards through the network, from input layer to output layer, in much the same way that activations are propagated.

items.title: Ceremonial etiquette and official events
items.abstract: Ceremonial etiquette plays an important role in diplomatic protocol and international relations. It regulates the conduct of diplomats and officials during official events and state ceremonies. Proper observance of ceremonial etiquette helps maintain order, respect, and professionalism in interactions between representatives of different countries. Official events such as state visits, diplomatic receptions, international conferences, and signing ceremonies follow specific traditions and protocol rules. These rules include the order of precedence, formal greetings, respect for national symbols, and appropriate dress code. The purpose of this study is to analyze the significance of ceremonial etiquette and its role in the organization of official diplomatic events. The research also highlights how adherence to ceremonial protocol contributes to strengthening diplomatic relations and preventing misunderstandings in international communication.

items.title: A Study on Filipino Protocol Officers in Diplomatic Ceremonial Events
items.abstract: This study explored the roles and challenges encountered by Filipino Protocol Officers in managing diplomatic ceremonial events. These officers played a vital role in ensuring the seamless execution of formal state functions and diplomatic interactions, balancing respect for tradition with the evolving demands of modern diplomacy. Using qualitative methods, including semi-structured interviews and document analysis, the research examined the officers’ preparation strategies, adherence to established protocol, and navigation of cultural nuances. Key findings underscored the critical importance of meticulous planning, cultural sensitivity, and effective inter-agency coordination. The study also identified major challenges, such as communication gaps, conflicting customs, and workload-related stress, along with the strategies employed to address them. Overall, this study contributed to a deeper understanding of the complexities involved in diplomatic protocol and offered recommendations for improving ceremonial event management practices in the Philippines.

items.title: THE ROLE OF PROTOCOL IN INTERNATIONAL RELATIONS AND PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION
items.abstract: The article examines the functions and role of state and diplomatic protocol and analyzes its theoretical foundations and practical application in international relations and public administration.The evolution of protocol from the court ceremonial of European monarchies to modern democratic state protocol based on the principle of sovereign equality of states is explored.It is demonstrated that protocol should be understood not merely as a set of etiquette rules but as a complex political and legal system that regulates official interaction, ensures predictability of diplomatic communication, and symbolically represents state authority in both international and domestic contexts.Three fundamental functions of modern protocol are identified and analyzed: regulatory, symbolic, and communicative.The regulatory function lies in establishing clear procedures and algorithms for organizing official meetings, negotiations, ceremonies, and other forms of diplomatic interaction, which helps prevent conflicts and misunderstandings among participants.The symbolic function manifests itself in the visual representation of state sovereignty, dignity, and legitimacy through the use of national symbols as well as ceremonial practices such as official visits and inaugurations.The communicative function is interpreted as a specific form of non-verbal political communication through which states transmit signals of respect, support, partnership, or, conversely, dissatisfaction and distancing in the international arena.Particular attention is paid to the transformation of modern protocol towar

items.title: The identifiable resolution of cellular counterfactual prediction — Source data
items.abstract: This record archives the numerical source data accompanying the manuscript “The identifiable resolution of cellular counterfactual prediction.” The study investigates context geometry compression (CGC), the dissociation between accurate cellular-state prediction and recovery of context-specific intervention effects. Its analyses distinguish measurement, information and prediction resolution. Key findings include limited context-specific recovery despite near-complete experimental coverage, greater recovery from pathway-level readouts of the same predictions, and saturation of functional personalization performance within a compact baseline-transcriptomic representation. The archive contains 20 figure source-data tables corresponding to Main Figures 1–6, Extended Data Figures 1–9 and Supplementary Figures 1–5, together with Supplementary Tables 1–6 in CSV and XLSX formats. It includes numerical estimates, uncertainty summaries, panel identifiers, source references, table captions, dataset accessions and resource-version information. Undefined quantities are retained as such, and metric definitions and statistical interpretations are documented in the accompanying files. These derived results originate from analyses of publicly available primary human CD4+ T-cell Perturb-seq data, official State cytokine and drug-response prediction artifacts, Tahoe-100M, paired lymphoblastoid cell-line data with independent ARCHS4 reprocessing, and colorectal-cancer organoid pharmacogenomic data. items.abstract: Verified Factual Reference Base and instrument registry, CWIAL No. 1, version 0.1.0 A reference base of propositions whose factual status has been verified against the documented record, with the sources supporting each verification and a registry of the survey instruments used to measure belief in them. It serves as the reference standard in belief displacement measurement: a displacement is only meaningful against a stated true value, and this file set holds those values, their evidential basis and their verification dates. Propositions are graded TRUE, FALSE or CONTESTED. This is not a catalogue of false claims. Contents. Three tables and their codebook. vfrb_propositions.csv holds the register, one row per proposition, with its truth value, evidential tier, verification dates and the basis for its assignment. vfrb_sources.csv holds the sources supporting each truth value, with a reliability grade and access date. instruments.csv holds the survey instruments used to obtain belief readings, with fieldwork date, documented bias and the base actually used. vfrb_codebook.csv defines every field of all three tables, with type, whether it is required, permitted values, and the five source reliability grade definitions. README, CHANGELOG, CITATION.cff and LICENSE complete the set. Inclusion criteria. items.title: The identifiable resolution of cellular counterfactual prediction — Analysis code
items.abstract: This record archives the analysis code accompanying the manuscript “The identifiable resolution of cellular counterfactual prediction.” The study identifies context geometry compression (CGC): models can preserve cellular identity and shared perturbation responses while failing to recover context-by-intervention interactions. It distinguishes measurement resolution, information resolution and prediction resolution, and examines the resolution at which cellular counterfactual responses are empirically recoverable. In the tested settings, high post-perturbation state accuracy and near-complete experimental coverage did not guarantee context-specific response recovery. The same predictions recovered more signal in pathway coordinates than in the full gene-expression vector, while compact baseline-transcriptomic representations retained most of the functional drug-ranking performance in patient-derived colorectal-cancer organoids. The archive contains 26 frozen scientific implementation bundles, configurations, split metadata, statistical resampling and null procedures, input requirements and execution documentation. These cover primary human T-cell prediction, official State prediction-artifact evaluation, Tahoe experimental completion and operator analyses, paired lymphoblastoid response prediction, pathway-resolution analyses, mechanism-aligned multimodal analyses and colorectal-cancer organoid personalization. items.title: Partial Order Semantics and Operational Semantics for Strand Spaces, via Rocq
items.abstract: Rocq mechanization accompanying "Partial Order Semantics and Operational Semantics for Strand Spaces, via Rocq" by Matteo Busi, Riccardo Focardi, Joshua Guttman, and Flaminia Luccio, submitted to JLAMP. This release extends the StrandsRocq framework with: an inductive characterization of bundles, with soundness and completeness theorems; a CPSA-style protocol syntax embedded in Rocq; a structured operational semantics for protocol execution; correspondence theorems showing that reachable thread pools and bundles carry exactly the same information; a computational labeled semantics, including the realization of compatible enumerations. items.title: turkish-llm-watermarking: code and data for TR-WM-EVAL, a Turkish watermark-evaluation benchmark
items.abstract: Archived snapshot of the repository behind the study Watermarking Turkish LLM Output: Detector Calibration, Scheme Fragility, and a Released Evaluation Benchmark . It contains the analysis code, the corpora, the detector scores and the judge annotations from which every number in that paper is regenerated. TR-WM-EVAL , the released benchmark, consists of 4,000 human text windows (1,500 Turkish Wikipedia, 1,500 word-matched English Wikipedia, 1,000 Turkish Wikisource), 384 generated Turkish texts, 3,840 attacked texts across ten removal attacks, 58,161 detector scores including a length-controlled rescoring and an eight-key sweep, and 788 pairwise LLM-judge verdicts. Its known limitations are stated up front in BENCHMARK.md: one generator, one watermark key on the attack axis, EXP's structurally fixed-length texts, judge verdicts covering only the KGW arm, and windows matched on words rather than tokens. Read DATA_LICENSE.md before reuse. The archive-level licence field is set to "Other (Open)" because no single identifier describes this deposit: it is not a blanket grant, and the per-path manifest in DATA_LICENSE.md is authoritative. Determine the applicable terms from the component you actually reuse. Components carry different terms: Wikimedia-derived text is CC BY-SA with a ShareAlike obligation that propagates to adaptations, round-trip translations are labelled CC BY-NC under a deliberately restrictive reading, generated and laundered texts and judge verdicts are CC BY 4.0, scores and metrics are CC0, and code is Apache-2.0. items.abstract: JEUNESSE INTEGRATION SOLIDARITE REPUBLICAINES (J.I.S.R LE PONT) L’association Jeunesse Intégration Solidarité Républicaines (J.I.S.R – Le Pont) est une organisation socio-culturelle active, fondée le 7 juillet 1995 et officiellement publiée au Journal Officiel le 2 août 1995. Elle est coordonnée par le professeur universitaire Dr. Hedi Saidi. Depuis sa création, l’association œuvre pour la promotion de l’intégration sociale, de la solidarité républicaine et du dialogue interculturel, en mettant l’accent sur la jeunesse et la cohésion communautaire. Basée à Villeneuve-d’Ascq (59650), l’association intervient dans le domaine de l’action socio-culturelle, en développant des projets destinés à renforcer les liens sociaux, favoriser l’inclusion, soutenir les initiatives éducatives et encourager la participation citoyenne. Elle agit comme un pont entre les différentes communautés, contribuant à la construction d’un espace social fondé sur le respect, la solidarité et les valeurs républicaines. Administrativement, l’association est enregistrée au Répertoire National des Associations sous le numéro RNA W595003926. items.title: Contract-typed faculty speech disclosures and university council investment mandates: A staggered-difference design estimating governance effects on academic-freedom violations in Ghanaian public universities
items.abstract: Ghanaian public universities combine strong constitutional protection for expression with council-centred control over finance and employment, creating a setting where speech regulation and investment authority interact in poorly understood ways. Drawing on institutional and accountability theory and on the recent staggered difference-in-differences literature, the framework proposes how variation in the timing of disclosure duties and investment mandates across universities would permit estimation of governance effects on recorded academic-freedom violations without requiring premature causal claims. The protocol specifies constructs, comparison groups, timing assumptions, measurement strategies using administrative and documentary sources, and diagnostics for heterogeneous effects and parallel-trends violations. The contribution is a bounded, implementable architecture for credible future inquiry into how employment and financial governance shape governed liberty in Ghanaian higher education.

items.title: From Victorian England to the Twenty-First Century: Reassessing the Contemporary Relevance of George Bernard Shaw's Mrs. Warren's Profession
items.abstract: George Bernard Shaw’s Mrs. Warren’s Profession remains one of the most controversial and intellectually engaging plays in modern English literature because of its penetrating critique of capitalism, patriarchy, class inequality, and Victorian moral hypocrisy. Although written in 1893 and first performed publicly in 1902, the play continues to resonate with twenty-first-century societies confronting persistent problems such as economic inequality, gender discrimination, labour exploitation, commercialized sexuality, and institutional hypocrisy. This article examines the enduring relevance of Shaw's social criticism by exploring the complex relationship between poverty, gender, morality, and capitalism in Mrs. Warren's Profession. Drawing primarily on Marxist literary criticism and feminist literary criticism, the study argues that Shaw challenges conventional notions of morality by exposing the structural conditions that compel women to adopt socially condemned occupations for economic survival. Rather than presenting prostitution merely as an individual moral failing, Shaw situates it within the broader framework of exploitative capitalist relations and patriarchal oppression. The article further demonstrates that many of the issues dramatized in the play continue to define contemporary societies across both developed and developing nations, thereby reaffirming literature's enduring capacity to illuminate persistent social contradictions. items.title: The Significant Push and Pull Factors Responsible for Migration of Africans (JAPA) Syndrome: The Comparative Analyses
items.abstract: This study investigates the endogamous and exogamous variables that represent African migration and the contemporary Nigerian Japa Syndrome. It contends that, beyond the unfavourable economic climate and the lingering security issues, among other internal vices in Africa, especially in Nigeria, the current trend of out-migration bears a connection with the neoliberal structure of European countries and emerging global trends. The paper aims to clarify the problem: the Old Testament agenda of migration of Africans in connection, relationship, link and association with the new trend of Japa syndrome and emotions, though Africa’s migration history involves and includes the movement of Homo sapiens, that is, the primate species to which modern humans belong, within and out of Africa. The primary objective of this research is to understand that Homo sapiens spread across Africa about 145,000 years ago and that some of those genes moved out of Africa 65,000 years ago. Moreover, major historical findings suggest that travel and migration have been a way of life in Africa, as they are today; according to United Nations estimates, about 50% of all African migrants live outside the continent. Theoretically, the number of documented refugees within the African region has doubled in recent years, continuing a 2-decade trend of expansion and enlargement. In this study, the primary push factors and influences for African migration are war and conflict, limited economic opportunities, and repressive governance back home.
